title: Galatians
summary: Galatians is a biblical book focused on justification, promise, law and gospel, Spirit, freedom, and new creation.
historical_context: Galatians defends the gospel of grace and explains freedom in Christ through promise and Spirit.
ancient_near_east_context: Galatians belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: Galatians should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received Galatians as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Pauline Epistles, book 4 of 13, Galatians contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting justification, promise, law and gospel, Spirit, freedom, and new creation to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read Galatians as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: Galatians uses epistle within Pauline Epistles, book 4 of 13 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: Galatians helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Traditional Pauline authorship or Pauline circle attribution
Critical scholarship debates several letters and recognizes co-workers in some correspondence
date_ranges: Some disputed letters are placed later or in the Pauline school
original_audience: Mixed Jewish-Gentile congregations and church leaders across the Roman world
historical_setting: The Greco-Roman world of mission, patronage, and local house churches
canonical_role: Galatians anchors justification, promise, law and gospel, Spirit, freedom, and new creation within Pauline Epistles, book 4 of 13 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
interpretive_disputes: How doctrine, ethics, and pastoral counsel fit together

related_objects.notes: Paul frames the letter's gospel defense.
Justification is a central theological concern.
The letter contrasts law and gospel within promise.
Faith is central to receiving the promise.
Life by the Spirit shapes the ethical exhortation.

scripture_references.notes: freedom and life by the Spirit

interpretive_notes.note: Read Galatians first within its own literary setting before moving to broader canonical connections.
